Starlink figured it out and stopped it.

cd.t: NO BOND: 5th Circuit Says Illegals Stay Locked Up: Part 2

items.tx:
NO BOND: 5th Circuit Says Illegals Stay Locked Up: Part 2

LIVE RIGHT NOW! 

Can an illegal alien who has lived here for twenty years demand a bond hearing and release from custody as matter of Constitutional right before ICE can hold him?

Yesterday the full Fifth Circuit, sitting en banc, ruled that the alien had a right under habeas corpus to the procedural step of having a court consider the question, but no substantive legal right to bond and release if Congress had ruled otherwise—and in the case of aliens unlawfully in the United States, Congress HAD ruled otherwise.

In Rodriguez v. Vergara, Judge Cory Wilson wrote for the majority, reversing two Western District of Texas judges who had ordered detained aliens released.

Those two trial judges, and a divided three-judge panel, found a Fifth Amendment right to a bond hearing, and the panel even invented a 90-day deadline.

The en banc majority vacated all of it, holding that while aliens are entitled to the right of habeas corpus, habeas is a procedural matter limited to having the question of release answered by a court, it is not a guarantee of liberty within our borders. The substantive question of release on bond is a separate statutory matter.

Seven judges dissented.

So is the majority correct that the Constitution guarantees the PROCEDURE of habeas, but leaves the SUBSTANCE of release on bond to Congress, not the courts?

In the preceding show, Part 1, #1492, I walked you through the majority opinion, explain the reasoning that decided it, and tell you what it means for the next ICE detention fight.

In this show, #1493, I do a Part 2 and work through two excellent concurrences, including a deep history lesson on the doctrine of habeas corpus. 

LIVE RIGHT NOW!
